extracted.intended_audience: readers and practitioners interested in maritime surveying, natural history, and 19th-century travel narratives (naval officers, surveyors, naturalists, colonial administrators, general Victorian readers)
extracted.subtask_description: Producing a first-person 19th-century maritime travel / natural-history narrative that combines coastal surveying (charts, soundings, bearings), natural-history collection and description, ethnographic vocabulary collection, and practical seafaring advice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anchorages exposed to easterly winds — timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Should a vessel be brought by any chance to this dreary part of the world in May, June, or July, anchorages exposed to easterly winds should be left at or before daylight--that being the time they set in; by noon all is again quiet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical navigational rule: depart such anchorages before the easterly winds establish (at or before daylight) to avoid being exposed to sudden easterly gales later in the day.

rubrics_metrics.name: Careful charting and positional determination
rubrics_metrics.description: The material for the chart collected in this part consists of the main from below Picard Island to nearly twenty miles west of Cape Lambert... Our object had been satisfactorily attained, inasmuch as we had cleared up the doubts respecting Ritchie's Reef, and the long-lost Tryal Rocks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey standard: obtain repeated observations (sights, chronometer checks), examine islands and reefs in detail, resolve discrepancies with existing charts, and publish corrected positions; include footnoted coordinates where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sounding methodology — search and conclude absence
rubrics_metrics.description: Our inducement to search for this shoal was ... But after searching from the 9th to the 14th, and sounding repeatedly without getting bottom, we came to the conclusion that it did not exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a reported shoal is suspected in a navigation route, conduct a systematic multi-day search and repeat soundings; if frequent soundings in the area show no bottom or no shoal features, conclude non-existence and record negative result.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record tidal streams and current rates
rubrics_metrics.description: The tide was ebbing and setting to the North-North-East two knots an hour.... the flood-stream came from the northward.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey practice: note direction and speed of tidal streams at anchorage and channels (knots/hour) and record timing (high-water at full and change). Use these to determine safe navigation routes and to explain vessel set.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use prominent land bearings to lead through channels
rubrics_metrics.description: We noticed that a hill, ... called Round-backed Hill, bearing between South 5 degrees East, and South 15 degrees East, clears the reefs on either side the channel; and that the same hill bearing South 24 degrees West leads between Bezout and Delambre, and South 8 degrees West clears the reef off the eastern side of the latter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Navigation technique: identify and record bearings of conspicuous hills or landmarks that, when held, lead clear of dangerous reefs; publish these bearings as practical leading marks for future pilots.

rubrics_metrics.name: Erect beacons as leading marks
rubrics_metrics.description: We again visited Rottnest ... for the purpose of erecting beacons on the rocks lying off the points of Thomson's Bay, as marks for leading clear to the eastward of the Champion Rock.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maritime-safety recommendation: install physical marks (beacons) on hazardous rocks/points to provide visual guidance for pilots; record their positions and the practical benefit to colonists and shipping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chart outputs should include tables of soundings with bottom quality and distance
rubrics_metrics.description: The following table is the result of other outer soundings obtained in the Beagle, showing how far the bank of soundings extends off the Western coast of Australia. COLUMN 1: LATITUDE SOUTH ... COLUMN 3: QUALITY OF BOTTOM. COLUMN 4: DISTANCE FROM NEAREST LAND.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mapping standard: when publishing survey results provide tabulated soundings (latitude, depth in fathoms), quality/type of bottom, and distance from nearest land so mariners can assess holding ground and proximity to shore.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meteorological observation and relation to lunar phase
rubrics_metrics.description: The weather has been truly strange ... In connection with our former remarks on striking vicissitudes in the weather occurring near the change of the moon, we should mention that it was new moon the day following.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include systematic notes on wind directions, veering, squalls, and any apparent correlation with lunar phase; such remarks help future voyagers anticipate local seasonal/stage-of-moon weather patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural-history specimen description and measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: Near Barrow's Island, on our passage, I shot (from the quarter-boat) the largest sea-snake ever killed. ... measured eight feet one inch in length, by three inches broad; the colour was a dark yellow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specimen standard: when collecting organisms record precise measurements (length, breadth), coloration, distinguishing morphological features, locality, and preserve specimens for later description and illustration (appendix references).

rubrics_metrics.name: Collection and naming of new species — descriptive standards
rubrics_metrics.description: We found a new kind of kangaroo ... From our description of this specimen it has been named Osphranter isabellinus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When encountering potential new species provide detailed morphological description, weights, coloration, habitat notes, and (if possible) bring specimens ashore; compare with known taxa and propose binomial names supported by descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethnographic vocabulary collection
rubrics_metrics.description: During the time he and his townsman Miago were with us, the following vocabulary was made; the words from Port Essington have been furnished by Mr. Earl.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When recording indigenous vocabularies: compile comparative columns (English / dialect A / dialect B), include animal and body-part terms, and cite informants and provenance; such lists should be made while informants are present and cross-checked where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caution and procedure in trading and contact with natives
rubrics_metrics.description: When a vessel arrives on the coast they flock down from the interior to trade, which cannot be done without an interpreter. It is even then attended with great risk, owing to the extreme treachery of the natives. ... they will not on any account allow them to live in their country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical safety guidance: use interpreters for trade, be wary of accepting hospitality ashore without security; recognize local reluctance to have Europeans settle and plan interactions accordingly (small trading items in demand: knives, stained blue, cotton goods).

rubrics_metrics.name: Voyage provisioning affects survey plans
rubrics_metrics.description: These winds prevented us from making the coast on the eastward of Depuch Island; and as we had failed in getting a supply of provisions at Timor, we were compelled to relinquish the plan of continuing the examination of that part of the coast between the Turtle Islands and Roebuck Bay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational planning rule: survey and exploration programmes depend on timely resupply; lack of provisions and adverse winds should trigger postponement or alteration of survey objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geological observation standards in coastal surveys
rubrics_metrics.description: The most remarkable feature is the absence or scantiness of the secondary and transition rocks; ... In most places about the neighbourhood of Fremantle, shells are found of the existing species along the coast, firmly impacted in its substance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When making geological notes record rock types, stratigraphic relations (e.g., tertiary over primary), presence and species of fossil shells, calcareous formations, and any evidence of past combustion/ignition on hill summits; indicate geographic extent of formations.
